title: Personal Credit Cards: Redeeming Points and Loss of Unredeemed Points
content:
This page governs how points held on Personal Credit Cards may be redeemed and the events on which unredeemed points are lost.

## Redemption

- Points are redeemed in whole points only, and each redemption must use at least the tier's smallest redemption.
- A redemption must use one of the ways the tier offers. A statement credit, which lowers the card's balance owed, and a gift card are each valued at the tier's cash worth per point; travel booked through the rewards center is valued at the tier's travel worth per point.
- The dollar value of a redemption is the number of points multiplied by the applicable worth per point, rounded half-up to the cent.
- Points may be redeemed only while the card account is active, as the bank's record of the account shows.

## Retired wording on deposit redemptions

The earlier wording of this rule listed “a deposit to a PCB checking or savings account of the same customer” among the redemption ways without any qualification. That unqualified wording is no longer in force: deposit redemptions are now governed by the current basis for deposits, which treats a cash-out made when a card is being closed differently from a deposit made at any other time. The tier's worth per point is unaffected by this change.

## Loss of unredeemed points

All points still unredeemed on the account are lost on any of these events:

- the account reaches the tier's forfeiture level of days past due;
- the account is charged off;
- the account closes.

Redemption is open only to an active account, and a confirmed closure wipes out whatever points remain; points still on a card when its closure is confirmed therefore can never be redeemed afterwards. Apart from these events, points never expire.

## Worked example (hypothetical figures)

A cardholder holds 8217 points on a tier whose smallest redemption is below that number, and asks for a statement credit of 8217 points at an illustrative worth of 0.009 USD per point: 8217 multiplied by 0.009 USD is 73.953 USD, which rounds half-up to 73.95 USD.

superseded_clauses: a deposit to a PCB checking or savings account of the same customer
